sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: In the Republican presidential primary, Nikki Haley is having a moment.
sentences.zh: 在共和党总统候选人初选中，妮基·黑利正迎来高光时刻。

sentences.en: The question is, what does it mean and where can it go?
sentences.zh: 问题是，这意味着什么，她又将走向何方？

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleagues, Jasmine Ayoa and Nate Cohn.
sentences.zh: 我与我的同事贾丝明·阿约亚和内特·科恩进行了交谈。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, December 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月7日，星期四。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's great to be here in Johnson County and great to be here in Iowa City.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到约翰逊县，也很高兴来到艾奥瓦城。

sentences.en: Jasmine, you have been covering the Nikki Haley campaign over the past many months.
sentences.zh: 贾丝明，过去几个月里你一直在报道妮基·黑利的竞选活动。

sentences.en: Every speech, every event.
sentences.zh: 每一场演讲，每一场活动。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you can help us understand what her candidacy was like when you first arrived on this beat.
sentences.zh: 我想请你帮我们了解一下，当你刚开始跑这条新闻时，她的竞选情况是怎样的。

sentences.en: So I first started trailing her in the summer.
sentences.zh: 我最早是在夏天开始跟随她的。

sentences.en: So I see some new faces and we appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 我看到了一些新面孔，我们对此非常感激。

sentences.en: So we're going to start off by telling you a little bit about me.
sentences.zh: 所以我们首先向大家介绍一下我自己。

sentences.en: And her crowds were modeSt.
sentences.zh: 当时她的人气并不高。

sentences.en: You know, I wouldn't say there were empty chairs everywhere, but they were definitely small.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我倒不是说到处都是空椅子，但人确实很少。

sentences.en: I'd look around in the press pen and there weren't that many reporters there yet.
sentences.zh: 我环顾记者席，发现那里还没多少记者。

sentences.en: So what I will tell you is if you've liked what I had to say today, go tell 10 people.
sentences.zh: 所以我想告诉大家的是，如果你喜欢我今天所说的话，去告诉10个人。

sentences.en: And the attitude from voters was excitement to see a conservative woman on this national stage.
sentences.zh: 选民的态度是，很高兴能在全国舞台上看到一位保守派女性。

sentences.en: Plenty of people knew her as governor of South Carolina or even more as a United Nations ambassador under Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 很多人知道她是南卡罗来纳州州长，或者更清楚她在唐纳德·特朗普手下担任联合国大使的经历。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: Good to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Hi, nice to meet you, Nikki.
sentences.zh: 嗨，很高兴认识你，妮基。

sentences.en: Yes, nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 是的，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: We're so glad you're here.
sentences.zh: 我们很高兴你能来。

sentences.en: Thanks for taking the time.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: But there didn't really seem to be a clear case for why she was running.
sentences.zh: 但当时似乎并不清楚她为什么要参选。

sentences.en: The attitude in the crowd was still very much like, why is she doing this?
sentences.zh: 人群中的态度依然很疑惑，觉得她为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: You know, I remember being in the audience and a voter very early on asking, is this going to be a repeat of 2016 where the field is just going to be fractured
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得当时在观众席中，很早就有选民问，这会不会是2016年的重演，当时候选人阵营四分五裂

sentences.en: and it's going to give Trump a chance to rise and don't you think people should drop out?
sentences.zh: 从而给特朗普提供了崛起的契机，难道你们不觉得其他人应该退选吗？

sentences.en: And the implication in the question was, don't you think you should drop out?
sentences.zh: 这个问题暗示的意思其实是，难道你不觉得你应该退选吗？

sentences.en: What you're describing and what this voter is really saying is that Nikki Haley at this point is kind of being written off.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的以及这位选民真正想表达的是，妮基·黑利在当时已经被看衰了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: She was single digits in the polls.
sentences.zh: 她在民调中只有个位数的支持率。

sentences.en: She was low on fundraising.
sentences.zh: 她的筹款也很少。

sentences.en: And that was especially putting her at a disadvantage in a place like Iowa, where it takes a lot of time and resources to really cover ground in the state.
sentences.zh: 这尤其让他在艾奥瓦州这样需要大量时间和资源来实地走访的地方处于劣势。

sentences.en: When did you start to notice all of that beginning to change?
sentences.zh: 你从什么时候开始注意到这一切开始发生变化的？

sentences.en: Tonight, the race for the White House takes flight.
sentences.zh: 今晚，白宫争夺战正式拉开帷幕。

sentences.en: Welcome to the first debate.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到第一场辩论。

sentences.en: I think the first inflection point for her campaign really was the first debate.
sentences.zh: 我认为她竞选的第一个转折点确实是第一场辩论。

sentences.en: This is exactly why Margaret Thatcher said, if you want something said, ask a man.
sentences.zh: 这正是玛格리特·撒切尔所说的，如果你想听人高谈阔论，去找男人。

sentences.en: If you want something done, ask a woman.
sentences.zh: 如果你想把事情办成，去找女人。

sentences.en: That's when she really stood out from the pack.
sentences.zh: 正是在那时，她真正从众多候选人中脱颖而出。

sentences.en: You have Ron DeSantis, you've got Tim Scott, you've got Mike Pence.
sentences.zh: 你有罗恩·德桑蒂斯，你有蒂姆·斯科特，你有迈克·彭斯。

sentences.en: They all voted to raise the debt.
sentences.zh: 他们都投票支持提高债务。

sentences.en: And at the next debate, she did even better.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的辩论中，她表现得更好了。

sentences.en: Honestly, every time I hear you, I feel a little bit dumber for what you say.
sentences.zh: 说实话，每次我听你说话，我都觉得你说的智商让我变低了一点。

sentences.en: She projected strength and confidence and experience.
sentences.zh: 她展现出了力量、自信和经验。

sentences.en: There you have it.
sentences.zh: 你看，就是这样。

sentences.en: Under your watch, you elect America.
sentences.zh: 在你的监督下，你选出了美国。

sentences.en: Let's say you have no foreign policy experience.
sentences.zh: 假设你没有任何外交政策经验。

sentences.en: And it shows.
sentences.zh: 而这也显露无遗。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: There's a foreign policy experience that you have.
sentences.zh: 你确实有一些外交政策经验。

sentences.en: And slowly and steadily, I started seeing more people at her events.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地、稳步地，我开始看到她的活动上有更多的人。

sentences.en: The makeup of the crowds was different.
sentences.zh: 人群的组成发生了变化。

sentences.en: She was reaching more independents, moderates.
sentences.zh: 她接触到了更多的独立选民和温和派。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: I was just in New Hampshire last week and I talked to voters.
sentences.zh: 我上周刚好在新罕布什尔州，我和选民交谈过。

sentences.en: Are you seriously considering Nikki Haley?
sentences.zh: 你是在认真考虑妮基·黑利吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: What about her?
sentences.zh: 她怎么样？

sentences.en: And when did you start considering her?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候开始考虑她的？

sentences.en: When did she come into your radar?
sentences.zh: 她是什么时候进入你的视线的？

sentences.en: Well, we watched the debates and everything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们观看了辩论以及所有这些。

sentences.en: And what I was hearing from people was that they really liked what she had to say at the debates.
sentences.zh: 我从人们那里听到的是，他们真的很喜欢她在辩论中的发言。

sentences.en: How many debates have there been?
sentences.zh: 已经举行了多少场辩论？

sentences.en: Two or three of them, right?
sentences.zh: 两三场吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: We watched all three.
sentences.zh: 我们看了全部三场。

sentences.en: She just, she shines.
sentences.zh: 她简直，大放异彩。

sentences.en: She has great presence.
sentences.zh: 她有着极佳的风度。

sentences.en: I've been impressed with how she handles herself.
sentences.zh: 她处理事情的方式给我留下了深刻印象。

sentences.en: And I think for the most part, she tells the truth.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为她在绝大多数时候都说的是实话。

sentences.en: You know, she talks about the deficit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她谈论赤字。

sentences.en: She's so pragmatic as far as abortion goes.
sentences.zh: 她在堕胎问题上非常务实。

sentences.en: They were really attracted to the way she talks about issues, especially abortion.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很喜欢她谈论议题的方式，尤其是堕胎问题。

sentences.en: I just think she sees the big picture.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得她有着宏观的眼光。

sentences.en: And a lot of people in politics want to be either far left or far right.
sentences.zh: 政坛中的很多人都想走向极左或极右。

sentences.en: And you can't, I don't think you can be that.
sentences.zh: 但你不能，我不认为你能那样做。

sentences.en: You've got to be somewhere in the middle.
sentences.zh: 你必须站在某个中间立场。

sentences.en: And I think she's more in the middle.
sentences.zh: 我认为她更偏向中间派。

sentences.en: I obviously wouldn't vote for Trump.
sentences.zh: 我显然不会投票给特朗普。

sentences.en: So it's down to a few people that sound a little bit more reasonable.
sentences.zh: 所以最终只能在几个听起来更理智的人当中选择。

sentences.en: Do you think that she can be the former president in the primary?
sentences.zh: 你认为她在初选中能击败前总统吗？

sentences.en: I don't know, but I'm wishing her the best of luck.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，但我祝她好运。

sentences.en: And how does this growing energy end up being reflected in those polls, which you said had been in just the single digits back in the summer?
sentences.zh: 这种不断高涨的势头是如何最终体现在民调中的呢？你刚才说夏天的时候民调还只有个位数。

sentences.en: So she's really surged in the early states, you know, after being less than 10% in these early states.
sentences.zh: 她在早期州的民调支持率确实飙升了，你知道，在这些早期州的支持率曾不足10%。

sentences.en: She is now at 20%, nearly 20% in New Hampshire and South Carolina, where she is in solidly second place.
sentences.zh: 她现在在新罕布什尔州和南卡罗来纳州达到了20%，接近20%，稳居第二位。

sentences.en: And in Iowa, she's climbing.
sentences.zh: 在艾奥瓦州，她也在不断攀升。

sentences.en: She's reached Ron DeSantis.
sentences.zh: 她已经追上了罗恩·德桑蒂斯。

sentences.en: She's tied in some polls about 16% in the last poll in October.
sentences.zh: 在10月份的最新民调中，她的支持率约为16%，与其他人不相上下。

sentences.en: And that steady climb in the polls, the breakout performances, and then the fact that you had former vice president Mike Pence and Senator Tim Scott,
sentences.zh: 民调的稳步上升、突破性的表现，再加上前副总统迈克·彭斯和同为南卡罗来纳州人的参议员蒂姆·斯科特

sentences.en: who was a fellow South Carolinian, dropped their bids this fall.
sentences.zh: 在今年秋天宣布退选。

sentences.en: All of these things have kind of led up to her seeing not only a rise in enthusiasm on the trail, but this rise in donations.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素共同作用，不仅让她在竞选活动中的热情高涨，也带来了捐款的增加。

sentences.en: And she's really caught the attention of more affluent donors, more, you know,
sentences.zh: 她确实吸引了更多富有捐赠者的注意，你知道的，更多

sentences.en: Wall Street executives have really warmed up to her.
sentences.zh: 华尔街高管对她展现出了热情。

sentences.en: And on top of all of that, she has attracted the attention of one of the most influential Republican donors,
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，她吸引了最具影响力的共和党捐赠者之一的注意，

sentences.en: billionaire David Koch, whose network, Americans for Prosperity Action, just last week endorsed her.
sentences.zh: 亿万富翁大卫·科赫，他的网络“美国繁荣行动”就在上周公开支持了她。

sentences.en: And this is one of the largest grassroots organizations out there.
sentences.zh: 这是现存规模最大的基层组织之一。

sentences.en: And they basically came out backing her, saying that she was the most electable candidate.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上公开表示支持她，称她是获胜希望最大的候选人。

sentences.en: And not only that, saying that she's a tested leader with the right judgment and the policy background to really turn the page on the divisive politics of the moment.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，还称她是一位经受过考验的领导人，具备正确的判断力和政策背景，能够真正翻过当下分裂政治这一页。

sentences.en: And that endorsement means that all that organization's money, all of its political muscle is suddenly behind Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 这一背书意味着该组织的所有资金、所有的政治力量突然间都成了妮基·黑利的后盾。

sentences.en: And it really seems to cap this pretty remarkable transformation from a candidate who can't really fill a room,
sentences.zh: 这似乎为她带来了一场相当惊人的蜕变：从一个甚至无法填满一个房间、

sentences.en: isn't covered by a lot of national reporters, and is in the single digits, to what Nikki Haley is now, at the close of 2023,
sentences.zh: 没有多少全国记者报道、民调只有个位数的候选人，变成了如今在2023年尾声时的妮基·黑利，

sentences.en: which is a candidate who looks like pretty much the number two in this race across many of these early voting states.
sentences.zh: 一个在许多这些早期投票州看起来几乎是这场竞选二号人物的候选人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, within a week of that endorsement, the organization had already poured $3.5 million into hiring door knockers and placing digital ads.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在该组织背书后的一周内，他们就已经投入了350万美元用于雇佣敲门拜访人员和投放数字广告。

sentences.en: So that really is going to change the game for her on the mobilization front, because this is a candidate who now has hundreds of volunteers in each of these early states.
sentences.zh: 因此，这确实将彻底改变她在动员方面的游戏规则，因为现在的这位候选人在每个早期州都拥有数以百计的志愿者。

sentences.en: And so it's been quite a few months for her, and it's been pretty remarkable to watch her climb from such a low position in the race
sentences.zh: 所以在过去的几个月里，她经历了很多，看着她从竞选中的低谷一步步攀升

sentences.en: to this strong challenger representative of people who want something other than Trump.
sentences.zh: 成为渴望特朗普以外选择的民众的强有力挑战者代表，这着实令人惊叹。

sentences.en: So Nate, as Jasmine just explained, Nikki Haley's success over the past few months is both undeniable and mathematically quite impressive.
sentences.zh: 内特，正如贾丝明刚才所解释的，妮基·黑利过去几个月的成功是不可否认的，而且在数学层面上也相当令人瞩目。

sentences.en: And now we want to turn to you to put it into context.
sentences.zh: 现在我们想请你将其置于更大的背景下来看。

sentences.en: So help us understand what Haley's surge means and doesn't mean in a race that is so thoroughly dominated by Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 请帮我们理解，在被唐纳德·特朗普全面主导的选战中，黑利的势头意味着什么，又没有意味着什么。

sentences.en: I think that what Nikki Haley is doing is she has positioned herself as the best candidate for voters who do not want Donald Trump to be the Republican nominee for president.
sentences.zh: 我认为妮基·黑利所做的是，她将自己定位为不希望唐纳德·特朗普成为共和党总统候选人的选民的最佳人选。

sentences.en: And Donald Trump is the clear front runner in this race.
sentences.zh: 而唐纳德·特朗普显然是这场竞选中的领跑者。

sentences.en: A majority of Republicans want him to be the nominee, but many do not.
sentences.zh: 多数共和党人希望他成为候选人，但也有许多人并不希望如此。

sentences.en: And what Nikki Haley is doing is something that's actually really common in presidential primaries.
sentences.zh: 妮基·黑利现在所做的事情，在总统初选中其实非常普遍。

sentences.en: And if I could use a fancy term for it, that term would be to call her a factional candidate.
sentences.zh: 如果我可以借用一个高大上的专业术语，这个词就是叫她“派系候选人”。

sentences.en: That's a candidate that appeals squarely to the wants and needs of a faction of a political party that is dissatisfied with the front runner of their own party.
sentences.zh: 所谓派系候选人，就是指那些完全迎合政党内部对本党领跑者感到不满的某一派别诉求和需求的候选人。

sentences.en: And if you think about it, even the strongest front runners, a George W.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，即使是最强大的领跑者，比如2000年的小乔治·W·布什、

sentences.en: Bush in 2000, a Ronald Reagan, a Hillary Clinton, don't perfectly appeal to everybody.
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根、希拉里·克林顿，也无法做到完美迎合所有人。

sentences.en: And as a result, there is almost always an opening for the candidate that appeals most directly to that disaffected faction of a party.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于那些最直接迎合政党中不满派别的候选人来说，几乎总是存在着机会之窗。

sentences.en: And in this election, that's Nikki Haley.
sentences.zh: 而在这次选举中，这个人就是妮基·黑利。

sentences.en: OK, well, remind us of some of the historical factional candidates because I think that might be illuminating.
sentences.zh: 好的，请提醒我们一些历史上的派系候选人，因为这可能会给我们带来启发。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders appealing to the Democratic Socialist left against a establishment moderate like Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 比如伯尼·桑德斯迎合民主党社会主义左翼以对抗像希拉里·克林顿这样的建制派温和派。

sentences.en: Rick Santorum appealing to the religious right against a establishment Mormon from the Northeast like Mitt Romney.
sentences.zh: 里克·桑托勒姆迎合宗教右翼以对抗像米特·罗姆尼这样的来自东北部的建制派摩门教徒。

sentences.en: John Kasich in 2016, the establishment moderate in that election against Donald Trump and Ted Cruz.
sentences.zh: 2016年的约翰·卡西奇，在那场选举中作为建制派温和派对抗唐纳德·特朗普和特德·克鲁兹。

sentences.en: Howard Dean, Ron Paul, Jesse Jackson.
sentences.zh: 霍华德·迪恩、罗恩·ポール、杰西·杰克逊。

sentences.en: we could do this for almost every election that there is a candidate who speaks to the needs of a part of the party that isn't satisfied by the front runner and in some cases is outright opposed to the front runner.
sentences.zh: 几乎每一次选举我们都可以这么说，都会有一位候选人，他代表了政党中对领跑者不满意、甚至在某些情况下公开反对领跑者的那一部分人的诉求。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A way to think about factional candidates as a result might be to see them as repositories for voters' disillusion with their party's front runner.
sentences.zh: 因此，看待派系候选人的一个角度，或许可以把他们看作是选民对本党领跑者幻灭情绪的寄托容器。

sentences.en: That's half of it.

sentences.en: But it's worth remembering that they usually have organic and authentic appeal to these same voters too.
sentences.zh: 但同样值得记住的是，他们对这些选民也往往有着天然且真实的吸引力。

sentences.en: You know, Jesse Jackson is not just a candidate who is there for black voters who don't like Michael Dukakis.
sentences.zh: 你知道，杰西·杰克逊不仅仅是一个为了那些不喜欢迈克尔·杜卡基斯的黑人选民而存在的候选人。

sentences.en: He had a real connection with left-linging voters and African-Americans in the 1984 Democratic primary.
sentences.zh: 在1984年的民主党初选中，他和左翼选民以及非裔美国人有着真实的联系。

sentences.en: Rick Santorum had real appeal to evangelicals.
sentences.zh: 里克·桑托鲁姆对福音派有着真实的吸引力。

sentences.en: He's not some faker.
sentences.zh: 他可不是什么骗子。

sentences.en: Bernie Sanders is a real appeal to Democratic socialists.
sentences.zh: 伯尼·桑德斯对民主社会主义者有着真实的吸引力。

sentences.en: He's a true believer.
sentences.zh: 他是坚定的信仰者。

sentences.en: And they usually have both of those traits.
sentences.zh: 而且他们通常具备这两个特质。

sentences.en: OK,
sentences.zh: 好的，

sentences.en: so how has Nikki Haley become the factional candidate success story in this Republican primary in such a crowded field where we anticipated that so many other Republicans might fill that role and where she herself is a somewhat complicated figure,
sentences.zh: 那么，在这样一个竞争激烈、我们原本预计会有很多其他共和党人来填补这一角色、且她本人也是一个有点复杂的人物初选环境中，妮基·黑利是如何成为共和党初选中派系候选人成功故事的呢？

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: She's a former high-ranking member of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 她是特朗普政府前高级官员。

sentences.en: I think you're right that she's a complicated figure.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你说得对，她是一个复杂的人物。

sentences.en: But I think that if you step back and look at her whole career,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得如果你退后一步，审视她的整个职业生涯，

sentences.en: that she really does embody a more traditional kind of conservatism that's really at odds with the Trumpist brand of Republican politics that we've seen over the last few years.
sentences.zh: 你会发现她确实体现了一种更传统的保守主义，这与我们过去几年看到的特朗普式共和党政治截然不同。

sentences.en: This is someone who when she ran and was elected as governor of South Carolina in 2010, she did support many conservative policies.
sentences.zh: 她在2010年参选并当选南卡罗来纳州州长时，确实支持了许多保守派政策。

sentences.en: But she also ran as the child of Indian American immigrants.
sentences.zh: 但她参选时的身份也是印度裔美国移民的子女。

sentences.en: And her defining moment as governor was ultimately deciding to support bringing down the Confederate flag from the state capitol in South Carolina after there was a mass shooting at a black church there.
sentences.zh: 她作为州长的高光时刻，最终是在南卡罗来纳州的一所黑人教堂发生大规模枪击事件后，决定支持将邦联旗从该州国会大厦降下来。

sentences.en: And it's worth remembering that she vigorously endorsed Marco Rubio in the Republican primary in 2016.
sentences.zh: 值得记住的是，她在2016年的共和党初选中强力背书了马可·鲁比奥。

sentences.en: And that even once she joined the Trump administration as UN ambassador, she was not exactly parroting the MAGA talking points about foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 甚至在她作为美国常驻联合国代表加入特朗普政府后，她也没有完全鹦鹉学舌般地重复那些关于外交政策的MAGA老调。

sentences.en: And so if you think about the things that anti-Trump Republicans are looking for in terms of temperament, in terms of views on the issues,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你回想一下反特朗普的共和党人在气质上、在对议题的看法上所寻找的特质，

sentences.en: and particularly on the issues that define Donald Trump, like his views on immigration, his populist economics, and his foreign policy,
sentences.zh: 特别是那些定义了唐纳德·特朗普的议题，比如他对移民的看法、他的民粹主义经济学以及他的外交政策，

sentences.en: Nikki Haley is exactly the kind of candidate they would be looking for.
sentences.zh: 妮基·黑利正是他们一直在寻找的那种候选人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're saying she's been able to carve out a political identity separate from Donald Trump, even though she served in his administration.
sentences.zh: 你是说她能够开辟出一种独立于唐纳德·特朗普的政治身份，尽管她曾在他的政府中任职。

sentences.en: I want to zero in on an example of that, how she has managed to seize on issues in a way that distinguish her from Trump in this current Republican primary campaign.
sentences.zh: 我想聚焦于其中的一个例子，看看她是如何在当前的共和党初选竞选活动中，通过巧妙抓住某些议题来使自己区别于特朗普的。

sentences.en: I think the easiest example is the way that she has talked about foreign policy in these debates.
sentences.zh: 我认为最简单的例子就是她在这些辩论中谈论外交政策的方式。

sentences.en: First of all, the American president needs to have moral clarity.
sentences.zh: 首先，美国总统需要具备道德清晰度。

sentences.en: They need to know the difference between right and wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们需要知道对与错的区别。

sentences.en: They need to know— And in particular, in these high-profile clashes with Vivek Ramaswamy.
sentences.zh: 他们需要知道——尤其是与维韦克·拉马斯瓦米的这些备受瞩目的交锋中。

sentences.en: And the problem that Vivek doesn't understand is he wants to hand Ukraine to Russia.
sentences.zh: 维韦克不明白的问题在于，他想把乌克兰拱手让给俄罗斯。

sentences.en: He wants to let China eat Taiwan.
sentences.zh: 他想让中国吞并台湾。

sentences.en: Who has been acting as sort of the MAGA candidate on stage without Donald Trump there.
sentences.zh: 在唐纳德·特朗普不在场的情况下，谁一直在舞台上扮演某种MAGA候选人的角色。

sentences.en: You don't do that to friends.
sentences.zh: 你不能对朋友做出这种事。

sentences.en: What you do instead is you have the backs of your friends.
sentences.zh: 相反，你要做的是坚定地支持你的朋友。

sentences.en: She has blasted Ramaswamy for being naive and not seeing the connections between Russia and China and Iran for his willingness to potentially reduce aid to Israel.
sentences.zh: 她猛烈抨击拉马斯瓦米过于天真，看不清俄罗斯、中国和伊朗之间的联系，并且愿意潜在地减少对以色列的援助。

sentences.en: A win for Russia is a win for China.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯的胜利就是中国的胜利。

sentences.en: We have to know that Ukraine is the first line of defense for us.
sentences.zh: 我们必须明白，乌克兰是我们防线的首要阵地。

sentences.en: And she has very vigorously defended all of the tenets of a neoconservative Reaganite foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 她非常坚定地捍卫了新保守主义里根派外交政策的所有信条。

sentences.en: Look at what Putin did today.
sentences.zh: 看看普京今天做了什么。

sentences.en: He killed Pergozian.
sentences.zh: 他杀了普里戈任。

sentences.en: This guy is a murderer.
sentences.zh: 这家伙是个杀人犯。

sentences.en: And you are choosing a murderer or a—
sentences.zh: 而你却在选择一个杀人犯，或者一个——

sentences.en: She's made this a defining issue for her in the campaign.
sentences.zh: 她把这变成了她在竞选中的标志性议题。

sentences.en: And this is an issue that a lot of people who dislike Trump really, really care about.
sentences.zh: 这也是许多讨厌特朗普的人非常非常关心的议题。

sentences.en: I just wanted to find a word that you have been using a little bit here, which is neoconservative.
sentences.zh: 我只是想探讨一下你刚才一直在使用的一个词，也就是新保守主义。

sentences.en: And correct me if I'm wrong, what you mean here is a foreign policy approach that harkens back to an older pre-Trump Republican tradition of being interventionist,
sentences.zh: 如果我理解有误请纠正我，你这里的意思是一种外交政策方法，它追溯到更早的、特朗普之前的共和党传统，即干涉主义，

sentences.en: seeing America's role as robust, elbows out, who needs us, where do they need us.
sentences.zh: 将美国的作用视为强有力的、强势的、谁需要我们、我们在哪里被需要的角色。

sentences.en: It's the opposite of Trump's more isolationist America-first approach to foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 这与特朗普那种更具孤立主义色彩的“美国优先”外交政策截然相反。

sentences.en: That's what you mean.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的意思。

sentences.en: Exactly, Michael.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，迈克尔。

sentences.en: And the key is that she is holding the flag that these neoconservative Republicans who have a long tradition in the Republican Party want to see pick up and held on a debate stage.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，她高举着一面旗帜，而这些在共和党内有着悠久传统的新保守主义共和党人，正渴望在辩论舞台上看到这面旗帜被捡起并高举。

sentences.en: What about domestic issues?
sentences.zh: 国内议题呢？

sentences.en: How has she distinguished herself from Trump and fueled herself as the factional candidate?
sentences.zh: 她是如何将自己与特朗普区分开来，并把自己塑造成派系候选人的？

sentences.en: So I think perhaps surprisingly abortion is the best answer to that question.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，出人意料的是，堕胎问题是这个问题的最佳答案。

sentences.en: Thank you, Martha.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，玛莎。

sentences.en: I am unapologetically pro-life, not because the Republican Party tells me to be.
sentences.zh: 我毫不掩饰地支持反堕胎，不是因为共和党叫我这么做。

sentences.en: She's pro-life, and she passed abortion restrictions as governor of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 她支持反堕胎，并且在担任南卡罗来纳州州长时通过了堕胎限制法案。

sentences.en: But she's been very skeptical about a federal abortion ban.
sentences.zh: 但她对联邦堕胎禁令一直非常怀疑。

sentences.en: When it comes to a federal ban, let's be honest with the American people and say it will take 60 Senate votes.
sentences.zh: 当谈到联邦禁令时，让我们对美国人民坦诚地说，这需要参议院60票的赞成。

sentences.en: It will take a majority of the House.
sentences.zh: 这需要众议院多数的支持。

sentences.en: So in order to do that, let's find consensus.
sentences.zh: 所以为了做到这一点，让我们寻找共识。

sentences.en: And she's argued instead, looking for consensus on the national stage on the issue.
sentences.zh: 她转而主张在国家层面上寻找关于这个议题的共识。

sentences.en: She's taking a respectful and conciliatory tone toward voters who are pro-choice.
sentences.zh: 她对支持堕胎权的选民采取了尊重和调解的语气。

sentences.en: And can't we all agree that we are not going to put a woman in jail or give her the death penalty if she gets an abortion?
sentences.zh: 难道我们不能都同意，如果一个女性堕胎，我们不会把她送进监狱或判处死刑吗？

sentences.en: Let's treat this like a respectful issue that it is and humanize the situation and stop demonizing the situation.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这当作一个它本来就值得尊重的问题来对待，让情况变得有人情味，停止妖魔化这种局面。

sentences.en: And I think that contrasts with the rest of the Republican field in a lot of important ways that appeal to voters who don't support Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与共和党其他候选人形成了许多重要的对比，从而吸引了不支持唐纳德·特朗普的选民。

sentences.en: A lot of people who are skeptical of Trump are relatively moderate, including on abortion, and there are a lot of pro-choice Republicans out there.
sentences.zh: 许多对特朗普持怀疑态度的人相对温和，在堕胎问题上也是如此，而且有很多支持堕胎权的共和党人。

sentences.en: But it's not just about the issues.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅关乎议题。

sentences.en: It's also about the tone.
sentences.zh: 这也关乎语气。

sentences.en: This kind of establishment-friendly, compromising, moderate, and conciliatory candidate is the sort of thing that a lot of voters want and are looking for.
sentences.zh: 这种对建制派友好、乐于妥协、温和且具有调解姿态的候选人，正是许多选民想要和寻找的类型。

sentences.en: And they may not be a majority of Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不是共和党人的多数。

sentences.en: But if you're the sort of person who doesn't like Donald Trump because of his conduct,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是因为唐纳德·特朗普的行事风格而讨厌他的人，

sentences.en: this is exactly the breath of fresh air that you're looking for from a Republican presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是你从共和党总统候选人身上寻找的一股清新空气。

sentences.en: But the conundrum for Nikki Haley, and really every effective factional candidate, is that the same things that make her appealing to independent moderate voters,
sentences.zh: 但对妮基·黑利以及实际上每一位有效的派系候选人来说，困境在于，正是那些让她对独立温和派选民产生吸引力的特质，

sentences.en: make her a really imperfect fit for the rest of a very conservative Republican party, and make it very challenging for her to actually beat Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 使她与其余极其保守的共和党人格格不入，也让她在实际击败唐纳德·特朗普时面临巨大的挑战。

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So Nate, walk us through why Nikki Haley's success at being a factional candidate so far means that it's going to be so hard for her to seriously challenge Trump.
sentences.zh: 内特，那么请给我们分析一下，为什么妮基·黑利目前作为派系候选人的成功，意味着她很难对特朗普构成真正的挑战。

sentences.en: Because I have to say, your description of what she has been up to so far seems like a plan to try to mop up every Republican voter who dislikes Trump,
sentences.zh: 因为我必须说，你对她目前所作所为的描述，听起来像是一个试图争取每一个讨厌特朗普的共和党选民的计划，

sentences.en: of which there are very many within the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 而在共和党内部，这样的人非常多。

sentences.en: There are a lot of them, but there aren't nearly enough of them to power a winning Republican presidential campaign, Michael.
sentences.zh: 确实有很多这样的人，但迈克尔，这些人数远远不足以支撑一场能赢的共和党总统竞选。

sentences.en: I mean, if we just step back and look at the math here for a second, there are three big blocks of Republican voters.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们退后一步，稍微看一眼这里的数学统计，共和党选民主要有三大板块。

sentences.en: One group, let's call it 40 percent of the Republican electorate, is the Trump MAGA base.
sentences.zh: 其中一个群体，我们可以称之为占共和党选民40%的特朗普MAGA基本盘。

sentences.en: They've supported him at every point.
sentences.zh: 他们在每一个关键节点都支持他。

sentences.en: They support him today.
sentences.zh: 他们今天依然支持他。

sentences.en: Then there's another 20 percent or so of Republicans that doesn't like Trump, disagrees on the issues strongly or disagrees with his personal character and conduct strongly.
sentences.zh: 然后大约还有20%的共和党人不喜欢特朗普，在议题上强烈反对他，或者极其反感他的个人品格和行事风格。

sentences.en: A lot of these people will consider voting for Joe Biden in the general election.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人在大选中会考虑投票给乔·拜登。

sentences.en: And Nikki Haley has a very good pitch for that 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 而妮基·黑利对这20%的选民有着非常好的说辞。

sentences.en: Then there's another 40 percent of Republican voters who like Trump but are open to voting for someone else.
sentences.zh: 接着还有另外40%的共和党选民，他们喜欢特朗普，但也对投票给其他人持开放态度。

sentences.en: Some of them like him a lot on the issues and don't like his personality as much.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人在政策上非常喜欢他，但没那么喜欢他的个性。

sentences.en: Some of them may like his personality but disagree with him on a few issues.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人可能喜欢他的个性，但在少数议题上与他意见不一。

sentences.en: And it's tempting to look at that 40 percent and say that those are voters that Nikki Haley can win over.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易看到这40%的选民，并认为这些是妮基·黑利可以争取过来的选民。

sentences.en: But they're much more conservative than the kind of independent moderate Biden curious Republicans or independents that Nikki Haley is often winning right now.
sentences.zh: 但他们比妮基·黑利目前经常争取的那些独立温和派、对拜登好奇的共和党人或独立选民要保守得多。

sentences.en: And the more that Nikki Haley does to secure her base of support among the people who don't like Donald Trump very much,
sentences.zh: 而且，妮基·黑利为了巩固她在那些不太喜欢唐纳德·特朗普的人当中的支持基础而做的事情越多，

sentences.en: the more she could repel the persuadable voters who do like Donald Trump and who support him on all kinds of issues.
sentences.zh: 她就越有可能排斥那些确实喜欢唐纳德·特朗普并在各种议题上支持他的摇摆选民。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: You're saying as Nikki Haley becomes known for becoming a Trump alternative and that message gets out more and more and she finds more and more ways to reinforce it,
sentences.zh: 你是说，随着妮基·黑利因成为特朗普的替代者而广为人知，这一信息越来越广为人知，且她找到了越来越多强化这一形象的方式，

sentences.en: she's going to be contrasting herself more sharply with Trump and therefore crystallizing for many Republican primary voters why they like Trump and why they don't like her.
sentences.zh: 她将与特朗普形成更鲜明的对比，从而为许多共和党初选选民明确指出他们为什么喜欢特朗普以及为什么不喜欢她。

sentences.en: In other words, the more she will push away that 40 percent who are a little wishy-washy on Trump and clarify for them why they might actually really like him.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，她越是这样做，就会把那40%对特朗普有些摇摆不定的选民推得越远，并向他们澄清为什么他们其实可能真的很喜欢他。

sentences.en: Yeah, many of these 40 percent think the Republican Party should oppose immigration reform.
sentences.zh: 是的，这40%的人中有许多人认为共和党应该反对移民改革。

sentences.en: Many of them oppose aid to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人反对援助乌克兰。

sentences.zh: 他拥有这样的奢侈条件，因为他在民调中遥遥领先，所以他可以把时间花在展望大选和接触——

sentences.en: Both Trump and Bush were pulling over 60 percent nationwide.
sentences.zh: 特朗普和布什在全国范围内支持率都超过了60%。

sentences.en: They had a lot of broad appeal in the Republican Party.

sentences.en: Bush wasn't running for a third Republican nomination, but it would be the third Bush Republican nomination.
sentences.zh: 布什不是在竞选第三任共和党提名，但这将是布什家族第三次获得共和党提名。

sentences.en: And John McCain at this time started out in the teens in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 而当时约翰·麦凯恩在在新罕布什尔州的支持率只有百分之十几。

sentences.zh: 布什的最强威胁之一。

sentences.zh: 布什州长，以及来自得克萨斯州的共和党参议员约翰·麦凯恩参议员。

sentences.en: And so what ended up happening?

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the most important thing that happened is that John McCain just kept gaining and gaining in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是说，发生的最重要的事情是约翰·麦凯恩在新罕布什尔州的支持率不断攀升。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I think we finally have a poll without a margin of error.
sentences.zh: 我想我们终于有了一个没有误差范围的民调了。

sentences.en: And McCain didn't just win New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 而且麦凯恩不只是赢了新罕布什尔州。

sentences.en: He won it big.
sentences.zh: 他赢得很大。

sentences.en: And we have sent a powerful message to Washington that change is coming.
sentences.zh: 我们向华盛顿发出了一个强有力的信息，即变革即将来临。

sentences.en: And it propelled him to a new level nationwide.
sentences.zh: 这推动他在全国范围内达到了一个新的水平。

sentences.en: He cleared the field of serious competition.

sentences.en: The other candidates got out.

sentences.en: And John McCain ultimately won seven states in the election, even though a few months earlier he had been losing 65 to 10 in the polls nationwide.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He caught fire.
sentences.zh: 他火了。

sentences.en: He caught fire.

sentences.en: He won a bunch of states.

sentences.en: But he didn't come especially close to winning the nomination.
sentences.zh: 但他离赢得提名并没有特别近。

sentences.en: And in the end, John McCain ran into the same problem that every factional candidate does,
sentences.zh: 最后，约翰·麦凯恩遇到了所有派系候选人都面临的相同问题，

sentences.en: which is that an appeal that is targeted at a faction of a political party and succeeds at consolidating it will often struggle to win over the majority of the party.
sentences.zh: 那就是，针对政党某一派系并成功将其整合的诉求，往往很难赢得党内大多数人的支持。

sentences.en: And he was unable to break that wall.
sentences.zh: 而他无法打破那堵墙。

sentences.en: So if we extrapolate from that example, Nikki Haley, if she replicates John McCain's success.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们从这个例子推断，妮基·海莉，如果她复制了约翰·麦凯恩的成功。

sentences.en: Which she is by no means assured to do.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是板上钉钉的。

sentences.en: But if she does, she might win New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 但如果她做到了，她可能会赢得新罕布什尔州。

sentences.en: She might quite logically win her home state of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 按常理她也很可能会赢得她的家乡南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: This is her best case, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这是她最好的情况，对吧。

sentences.en: She could go on and win seven states.
sentences.zh: 她可能会继续赢得七个州。

sentences.en: And it would probably create a real impression of success and viability as a challenger to Trump.
sentences.zh: 这可能会给人留下一种真实的印象，即她作为特朗普的挑战者是成功且具备竞争力的。

sentences.en: I'm saying this because I'm a journalist and we can often lose our bearings.
sentences.zh: 我这么说是因为我是个记者，我们有时会迷失方向。

sentences.en: But you're saying based on the math of being a factual candidate, based on the model of John McCain, it's very likely to then stall out.
sentences.zh: 但你是说，基于派系候选人的数学逻辑，基于约翰·麦凯恩的模式，接下来很有可能会陷入停滞。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, remember what's going on here, Michael.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，迈克尔，想想这里正在发生什么。

sentences.en: This is not a party of moderate establishment types anymore.
sentences.zh: 这已经不再是一个温和建制派政党了。

sentences.en: It's a very conservative and populist party.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常保守且民粹的政党。

sentences.en: And Nikki Haley is not a very conservative populiSt.
sentences.zh: 而妮基·海莉并不是一个非常保守的民粹主义者。

sentences.en: That fact is exactly what lets her win 20 percent.
sentences.zh: 这个事实正是她能获得20%支持率的原因。

sentences.en: And it's the same fact that means she will have a very hard time to be generous winning 50 percent.
sentences.zh: 同样也是这个事实意味着，客气点说，她要想赢得50%的支持率将极其艰难。

sentences.en: Is there any scenario where Haley could somehow shock everyone and do more than win seven states but keep going and truly become somehow competitive with Trump?
sentences.zh: 有没有任何可能，海莉能以某种方式震惊所有人，不仅赢得七个州，还继续前进，真正对特朗普构成某种竞争力？

sentences.en: Or is what you're saying, and maybe I'm just too dense, mathematically, Michael, that's just not possible.
sentences.zh: 还是说你的意思是——也许是我在数学上太笨了，迈克尔——这根本不可能？

sentences.en: So just shut that down.
sentences.zh: 所以别想这事了。

sentences.en: Well, let me just start with a historic answer, which is that these factional candidates almost always lose.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我先从一个历史角度的回答开始，那就是这些派系候选人几乎总是会输。

sentences.en: And the only time when these factional candidates win, like they almost show that they weren't factional candidates.
sentences.zh: 而这些派系候选人获胜的唯一时刻，就好像他们证明了自己不是派系候选人一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So if Nikki Haley were to win the nomination with the campaign that she's run to this point, it would be tantamount to demonstrating that she's not a mere faction,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果妮基·海莉能凭借她至今为止的竞选赢得提名，这就等于证明她不仅仅代表某个派系，

sentences.en: that the things that she believes and that she represents are actually much more broadly appealing in the Republican Party than I'm giving credit for today.
sentences.zh: 证明她的信仰和代表的主张在共和党内其实比我今天所承认的要具有更广泛的吸引力。

sentences.en: It would be an indication that much of what I've told you is wrong, not that she somehow overcame it.
sentences.zh: 这将表明我之前告诉你的很多内容都是错的，而不是她以某种方式克服了这些困难。

sentences.en: And if that happens, then, you know, we can have this conversation.
sentences.zh: 如果真的发生了，那么，你知道的，我们就可以进行这段对话了。

sentences.en: I've been wrong before.
sentences.zh: 我以前也错过。

sentences.en: Inferences based on polling have been wrong before, of course.
sentences.zh: 基于民调的推断以前也出过错，当然。

sentences.en: But historically speaking, for a candidate like Nikki Haley to win, it would be a sign that we're just wrong about the breadth of her appeal and of her faction today.
sentences.zh: 但从历史角度来看，对于妮基·海莉这样的候选人来说，要赢得胜利，将是一个信号，表明我们对她今天及其派系的吸引力范围的看法完全错了。

sentences.en: That said, in this particular election, there is this big asterisk about Donald Trump's legal challenges.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，在这场特定的选举中，关于唐纳德·特朗普的法律挑战有一个巨大的星号标记。

sentences.en: I think that we do have to continue to offer that caveat as the campaign gets underway.
sentences.zh: 我认为随着竞选的推进，我们确实必须继续提供这一警告。

sentences.en: Those challenges will become more real as he actually gets into a criminal trial.
sentences.zh: 随着他真正卷入刑事审判，这些挑战将变得更加真实。

sentences.en: I think we have to at least allow the possibility, however small, that this will change the race, even though it has not to this point.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们至少必须承认这种可能性（尽管很小），即这会改变竞选格局，尽管到目前为止还没有改变。

sentences.en: But other than that, you know, there's not really much of a reason to think that, you know,
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，你知道的，并没有太多理由认为，

sentences.en: a moderate establishment type figure in today's Republican Party is well positioned to win the Republican primary electorate.
sentences.zh: 当今共和党内的温和建制派人物有很好的条件去赢得共和党初选选民的支持。

sentences.en: It's just not what the Republican Party is.
sentences.zh: 共和党现在根本不是那样的政党。
